steps.content:
August 22, N.F. 115 22:00
Junction of DisSea and the Rust
FAC Broken Frontline
Siglinde's brow furrows.
Her eyes fix on the distant city. An unprecedented Tide of Ashes surges violently across the land, staining the air with the metallic tang of rust and the smell of scorched earth.

Yet more unnerving than the calamity ahead is the threat looming behind—from beyond the far end of the Broken Frontline. The Illusory Moon has not yet risen, but even through the anti-Mania barriers, she can hear the DisSea roaring.

The defensive line, built from the rubble of countless collapsed buildings, shudders endlessly as though battered by invisible beasts. In the shallows, reef rocks dissolve into a black, devouring sludge that consumes all it touches.
Hordes of Apostles push deeper along the Rust, using the river's polluted veil to dash forward. Outposts in their path fight desperately to hold, only to be overrun one by one.

Is this the enemy's final assault? Driving the Apostles from the front while stirring the depths of the DisSea from behind—a coordinated pincer attack on DisCity... The thought sends a cold sweat beading along Siglinde's temples.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: ...Should we request reinforcements? I could contact General Augustus and persuade her to provide assistance.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: No need. They're on another mission.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: But if the Apostles breach our defensive line, wouldn't the consequences be severe?

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Yes, but that's not going to happen.

Where does this old man get his unshakable confidence? Does he truly not care for the lives of his soldiers? With so many Apostles swarming the field, even ten lives per FAC soldier wouldn't be enough to hold the line. Unable to contain her curiosity any longer, Siglinde snatches up a telescope to survey the crumbling front.

The Apostles are gathering in ever-growing numbers, the majority already surging through the contaminated zone in a frenzied charge. Some powerful force is driving them—compelling them forward. Are there Aurum Secretum Warriors nearby?

Her gaze sweeps frantically across the battlefield, but she finds no trace of them. Those warriors' presence is always conspicuous, impossible to miss. She can't have overlooked them. And yet, the FAC's defenses at the end of the Rust are among their most fortified...

Wait... they were prepared for this? They knew the Apostles would cross the Rust. These fortifications... they're not just defenses. They were designed to funnel the hostiles right here, to keep them from spilling into the city?

steps.speaker: Apostle
steps.content: <size=52><color=#dg1f1f><i>—! —!!!!</color></size><i>
But the Apostles seem so erratic... so aggressively violent. She can't help but wonder what powerful force is compelling them to push this far.
A nearby FAC soldier takes the telescope from her hands and hands her an updated battle briefing.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Look, Aurum Secretum, Underground sorcery, all of it... it's just human ingenuity. But controlling Apostles? Truly controlling them? Never been done. If we could've, we'd have ended the catastrophes years ago.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: We've been fighting Apostles long enough to know their nature. They always have this desire to return to the DisSea. Even the thinnest crack in the walls around BR-000 is enough to trigger that instinct. They can't resist it.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: A plan like this... it would require detailed technical parameters on the resonance between Aurum Secretum and Apostles. Where did you acquire this intel? And when? The Ring Research Institute hasn't pursued this line of research.
Though the soldier's expression is hidden behind a mask, Siglinde senses an unmistakable air of smugness.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: It came from one of our intelligence assets in the farlands. One minute is more than enough for her to get many things done.

She studies the battle briefing, her mind returning to the brief, precious window before the final battle when DisCity's intelligence network at the farlands had flickered back to life. In that narrow gap, they had managed to tear a critical pocket of intelligence.
As for how they managed to tear an opening into the Mania dark web—
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: We've got a new lead. A captive brought back from WhiteSands, elite class at minimum, capable of manipulating Apostles with Aurum Secretum. During dispersed operations, these types will definitely communicate through the Mania dark web.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: She's been cautious in custody—no outgoing signals. But compared to Adelaide Campbell? This one's practically gift-wrapped. Keep close surveillance.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: It's our turn to play their game now. We'll piggyback on their own network. The moment she initiates contact, we trace and decrypt immediately. Even if we only have one minute, we must locate our missing agents in the farlands.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: After that... they'll finally become useful.
The spymaster's gaze was cold and steady on the screen. On the monitor, the Outland prisoner fled in a blind panic, utterly unaware she was already tracked.
[Flashback]
Selyna raced through the dim alleyways, finally stumbling to a halt in a secluded corner. She gasped for breath—not from exhaustion, but from the emotional tempest raging within her.

The thought of returning to camp with her mind so clouded by doubt was unbearable. She had always been unwavering, a pillar of conviction on the battlefield, never permitting herself the slightest hesitation... but now...

Gritting her teeth, she unleashed her ability. Her fingertips traced Aurum Secretum patterns, emitting a specific frequency. The power of Mania answered, transforming into a torrent of raw information that flowed into her mind.

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: Director... I'm out. I made it. But... I had to reach you. I can't just report to camp, not with this sickness in my thoughts. This war means everything to me. I can't move another step until I know the answer.

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: You're the one I trust the most, and I believe in your integrity... So please, for the sake of everything we're doing, tell me the truth. I need to hear it from you.

As the fragmented transmission left her, the memory crashed over her anew, a fresh wave of turmoil. That girl from DisCity, the one who'd aimed a gun at her hours ago... what was her name? El-something-ra...
No, that's wrong. She wasn't from DisCity... The correct name, the real identity... was Nysa Sadikur. Of Furor.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: My mother... she was from Furor. She made a deal with Fraser... to come here to DisCity. To get close to the Speaker. She even had me... just to make it look real. She kept that secret her whole life. She never broke her cover.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: But I know now... even more than she did. I know what you did... Fraser... set off a Black Ring right on top of Furor, her homeland! You wiped out every last one of her people! She gave you everything for a promise, and it was all a lie!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: You said this war was righteous revenge! You said it was for justice, for all Outlanders! She believed you her whole life! So what is that? What is that Black Ring right in front of us? Tell me!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Was she part of the plan, too? Was she just another thing to throw away when you were done with Furor?

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I thought... I thought her people were good. My people. I just wanted to help. I just wanted to understand you! But look what you did!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I know you betrayed my mother! After what you did... how can you even say words like "justice"?
Early during her interrogation by the 9th Agency, Elvira had already voluntarily offered to cooperate.

She pledged her full assistance in dismantling the Outland intelligence network—a proposal with conditions the agents, recognizing her capabilities, readily accepted. And the final results proved highly satisfactory.
When she heard Sibilla's story about Furor, a complete plan was formed instantly, built on her observation of the fanatical Aurum Secretum Warrior.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: She's a lost cause... Her mind's been warped into nothing but vengeance. She won't listen to reason. So to get her to talk... I have to speak the only language she understands... Identity and hatred.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: So I pretended to be one of her people, to plant that seed of doubt. A self-righteous zealot like her can't stand that. She'll be desperate for validation, for someone to confirm her so-called justice. We just have to see who she'd run to—their military camp outside the city, or if we get lucky...

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: If she starts doubting even her own comrades... maybe she'd try to contact someone in Fraser thousands of miles away...

Hiding in her small room at the Bureau to deliver her report, she clutched the little handgun she always carried. Leaning against the headboard, she spoke in a low, steady monotone amidst the dry clicks of the trigger.
It was a depth of calculation and cunning astonishing for a mere seventeen-year-old.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: The former Speaker, a Fraser spy... What a twisted family to breed such a dangerous talent.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: You played your hand well, Miss Stewart. Tell me, does this victory taste as sweet as you imagined?

A promising new talent, she noted with a smile to herself. As her hand swiped across the terminal, the encrypted message sent from Fraser decoded at last, revealing the long-absent symbol: the peace dove.
"The Senate's taken care of. Oh, and I pried some choice Aurum Secretum intel from a little Campbell scholar. Let's see if the FAC's gentlemen can actually put it to good use."
"Clock's ticking. The rats will pick up the scent soon, so I'm going dark. The rest is on you. I'm in no position to double back anyway. This is your turf, your play."
"And I think we both would rather not see they hit here with that disgusting thing in the sky."
[Broken Frontline]

Light indicators flicker across the sand table, tracing the paths of the remaining Apostle swarms as they flow from BR-005 toward the Rust, then onward to DisSea—only to be intercepted by the Broken Frontline. FAC's precise calculations ensure the defensive perimeter allows just enough controlled leakage to maintain a fragile balance.

Hypercube consumption continues to climb. The logistics department anxiously diverts resources from every available channel, including Nirvana. Once again, this "incomplete" force is being tested by fire, caught between impossible demands.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: See? Holding this line meant something. We buy that future, and someone else will take the chance and turn the tide.
The soldier says, his eyes fixed on the steadily rising monitoring feeds. The moment they reach the predetermined threshold, he rushes excitedly to the Commander-in-Chief to deliver the news.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Commander, civvies are clear. The gloves are off.
Siglinde glances toward the FAC's highest commanding officer. The old man remains absorbed in the sand table, yet he is unmistakably aware of her gaze.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Liaison Officer Siglinde, you don't actually trust FAC, do you? You're here primarily to gather intelligence.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: And you needn't worry. I understand. The schism in N.F. 103 created a rift that hasn't healed. In many ways, that makes your presence here more valuable. I also have messages I'd like to relay through you.
The old commander rises to his feet and makes his way toward the broadcasting station.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Unlike the old DisCorps, the FAC does not pursue war for its own sake or condone excessive force. We are not skilled at fighting human malice. We operate under constraints, stubbornly clinging to principles some see as weaknesses, unwilling to sacrifice others casually. And because of this, we cannot achieve the grand, sweeping victories others might.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: What you've witnessed in this war has left you disheartened. You doubt we can still fulfill our duty.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Do not make that mistake. Never forget where our real strength lies.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: We renounced killing because we made a conscious choice for life. We swore to bear its weight, to protect those in our care. That is not a limitation. That is the very source of our strength. And through it, we will become immeasurably strong.
The cacophony of the command center fades into a dull hum, drowned by the thunderous rumbles from the battlefield. Their rhythm is a key, unlocking memories long buried.
[Three DisCorps generations' portraits with black gradient]
Hearts waver and times change, yet some things must remain constant. He will be that constant.

Adrian Sterling—the Nirvana Port Commanding Officer of the Independence Army, the second Commander-in-Chief of the FAC—once more stands before the final line of defense, his voice cutting through the chaos with unwavering command.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Attention, all FAC stations. The Rust sector of the Broken Frontline will be opened for a precise window of 200 minutes. The enemy has weaponized the resonance between the DisSea and the Apostles. Now, we will turn their own weapon against them.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: We will give those monsters a taste of the true DisSea. Lure them in. Fight for control. Their Aurum Secretum and their pathetic Secondary Black Ring are no match for the power of the DisSea.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Our objective is to split their formation, isolate BR-005 completely, and carve a path for our allies. Prepare for simultaneous assaults from inside and outside the Broken Frontline. Holding the line against impossible odds is what we do!

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: They believe a Secondary Black Ring lets them command Apostles, disrupt the DisSea, and slaughter our people? Let those reckless warmongers bear witness.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Let them see the true face of the Mania we've been fighting all these years. Show them what a real catastrophe looks like!

steps.speaker: FAC Soldiers
steps.content: Yes, sir!!

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: As for you...
He turns to Siglinde.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Now go contact your general and tell her:

steps.speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: "FAC will fulfill its mission without fail. Now, it's <color=#fb9259>your</color> turn."
Siglinde snaps to attention and delivers the DisCorps salute to the FAC Commander-in-Chief.

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: Yes, sir. Consider it done.
